objective: Investigate recurring public FP8 eager setup and identify observed cuBLAS algorithm configurations and CUDA kernels, without changing production code, persistence or measurement policy.
execution_commit_rule: Run a clean committed checkout containing this plan and diagnostics; record exact source hashes per attempt. Qualification failures and fixes remain separate attempts. All three primary workers must use the same frozen execution commit.

workload.inputs: seeded FP8 e4m3fn tensors; fixed exact pointers/layouts within each worker; unit FP32 dequantization scales
workload.lookup: actual tuner in-memory winner lookup forced to -1 or ordinal0, with verified hits; zero profiling permitted
workload.persistence: unchanged production v1 path; no managed attachment; no new startup tuning in this focused mechanism experiment

protocol.qualification: one clean unpreloaded benchmark worker, seed17, two samples, same warmup/calibration; must pass before primary workers
protocol.primary_instrumentation: none: no LD_PRELOAD, boundary hooks or Torch profiler
protocol.variant_order: deterministic seeded shuffle in each fresh worker; record complete order
protocol.observation: one separate fresh seed17 worker with native preload and CPU boundary hooks; five eager calls, one capture, five replays per variant; separate CPU/CUDA traces with native recording disabled
protocol.compilation_caches: shared within batch; initial kernel and donor setup excluded from timing

acceptance: Actual CUDA-header probe build and all required workers exit successfully; retain failed attempts separately.
Exact pinned source/package/image/GPU provenance and immutable input/donor hashes pass.
All public variants consume the intended real cached winner; retained variants bypass tuner intentionally; zero profiling throughout.
All eager and poisoned-output/changed-input/restored-input graph checks pass.
Each primary timing has15 finite positive wall/event samples, at least500ms warmup and a calibrated batch of at least20ms; normalization matches raw batches.

Native interception is proven: unseeded public ordinal0 requests100 heuristic results, default requests1, seeded public ordinal0 and prepared retained ordinal0 avoid enumeration; graph replay has no native setup calls.
Record actual submitted algorithm bytes and supported configuration attributes, plus GPU kernel trace evidence; missing interception/activity is pending evidence rather than an inferred identity.
analysis: Use three paired worker-median ratios per execution mode; timing samples and variants are not independent trial replications.
Primary causal contrast is seeded-public ordinal0 versus unmodified public ordinal0. Seeded-public default is the intervention-overhead control.

The intervention preserves fresh runner construction and dispatch, replacing enumeration with an already-valid CPU list only for the fixed exact workload. Attribute its total effect to avoided list setup/allocation/query, not one native API in isolation.
Retained-runner comparisons remove multiple public/lookup/setup layers and do not alone isolate enumeration.
Native and Python host durations are perturbed nested observations; never add them together or treat them as uninstrumented latency.

Compare observed algorithm configurations and actual traced kernel names. Equal selected attributes/opaque bytes are not a universal proof of identical device behavior; raw-byte differences alone do not prove different algorithms.
The three-arm natural startup/performance comparison remains the separate preceding batch. This experiment diagnoses its mechanism rather than measuring a production optimization.

publication.retain: source, plan, launcher, probe build log/hash, exact commands, all JSON/logs/native events/compressed traces, failed attempts, independent analysis and checksummed byte-preserving raw archive; narrative in the existing single working record
